label: lad-61e79
summary: The network rates an opening Connect-4 position for x mainly by who holds the centre column, especially the bottom centre square d1, and reads the bottom row and the lower centre squares far more than the upper rows. On the training boards the mean predicted chance of an x win is 77% where x holds d1 and 54% where o holds it; holding d1 at its training average lowers the AUC from 0.9556 to 0.8897, against 0.9550 for the top centre square d6. The first layer turns the squares into piece-placement features; in the second layer some units detect x or o on the centre column or on single bottom squares near the edges and push the output up or down, one unit partly offsets an o piece on d1, and the rest are described by their closed form. The thresholds matter: with the second layer replaced by an affine fit the AUC is 0.8534.

recheck_summary.rule: an explanation cannot be marked complete with an unresolved mismatch; answer every needs_review item (fix it or say why it is not an error)

recheck_notes: Recheck: mismatch 0, needs_review 0. The free-text sentences it could not check are interpretive (Connect-4 readings) or structural (layer descriptions); every number in them is a placeholder resolved from a stored query.
tool_bugs: query_probe's hold takes 'row:N', not a bare row index (the error message says so). get_formula with force on the root and the second-layer composition took several minutes (hundreds of kB of LaTeX); the collapsed forms were attached instead. query_subgroup with a long or-expression of x three-in-a-row patterns returned n = None (the matching o queries returned 0); these queries are unused. split_node cannot split an input that feeds 32 units (26 letters), so the first layer could not be divided into several leaves.

refuted_and_fixed: win_vote: "moving a piece to d1 always moves the prediction towards its owner" was refuted by one probed board (o piece g1->d1 raised the x-win chance); rewritten as a tendency with the counterexample stated
second_layer_evidence: turning the d1 piece from x to o did not lower the prediction on one probed board because counterweight unit 47 switched on; the counterweight was added to the hypothesis

leaves.name: board_square_features
leaves.why: As a whole the layer makes the model depend on the bottom row and lower centre squares (self-probed by holding single squares at their average), but its units are not read one by one.

composition_parts.name: second_layer_evidence
composition_parts.why: Units 36, 39 (for x) and 42, 38, 46 (against x) detect who holds d1/d2, unit 41 is held off by o on d1, unit 47 offsets o on d1, units 43 and 45 fire on o pieces at b1 and a1 (for x), units 33 and 34 on x pieces at f1 and c2 (against x); the other five units have no reading.

composition_parts.name: win_vote
composition_parts.why: Sigmoid of a signed vote; moving a piece to d1 moves the prediction towards that piece's owner on the probed boards except one.

overall_function: The network values an opening Connect-4 position for x mainly by ownership of the centre column, especially the bottom centre square d1 and the square above it: x pieces there raise the predicted chance of a win and o pieces there lower it, while pieces on the edge columns go with the opposite tendency. It reads the bottom row and the lower centre squares far more than the upper rows, which are rarely filled in these positions. The interaction is mostly a set of second-layer threshold units that switch on when one player holds d1 (and d2), with a counterweight unit that partly cancels an o piece on d1, so the centre effect is a strong tendency rather than a rule. No unit examined was read as a detector of lines of four or of threats.
stuck: Structure: the dense net allows one leaf only (inputs cannot be split 32 ways), so the second layer lives in a composition. Meaning: the first-layer units and five second-layer units have no domain reading in the time box. Tools: get_formula on the composition and root was slow.
